title: Bull's Blood and Noble Rot: Seven Days Between Eger and Tokaj
subRegion: Eger and the Bükk foothills, then Tokaj-Hegyalja on the Bodrog

bestPeriod.window: the last week of September through the third week of October, Eger's reds are in, Tokaj's aszú pickers are out
bestPeriod.avoid: December-March (many Hegyalja cellars open by appointment only, and the Szépasszony-völgy row half-shuts)

accommodation.note: €380, €640 (€55, €92/night; Eger guesthouse plus a Mád or Tarcal manor)

activities.note: €190, €330 (cellar visits €15, €60; an aszú vertical runs higher)

hook: Two Hungarian wine regions, three hours apart, that share almost nothing. Eger is rhyolite tuff, Kékfrankos, and a horseshoe of cellar doors cut into a valley wall where you drink standing up. Tokaj is loess over volcanic rock, grey mould furring the cellar ceilings, and sweet wine measured in *puttony* baskets. Come in October: the Bükk turns copper, aszú pickers work berry by berry, and the cellars smell of fermenting must and damp stone.

snapshot.Best period: Late September to mid-November; aszú picking runs into November
snapshot.Start / End: Budapest → Eger (3 nights) → Tokaj-Hegyalja (4 nights) → Debrecen or Budapest
snapshot.Getting there: Budapest Liszt Ferenc (BUD) then hire car; Eger is 130 km northeast, about 1 h 50 on the M3. Rail: Budapest Keleti-Eger, roughly 2 h with a change at Füzesabony. Leaving from Tokaj, Debrecen (DEB) is ~100 km and often cheaper than driving back to Budapest.

itinerary.title: Eger: Castle, Minaret, Cellar Row
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at BUD and drive the M3 to Eger. Buy the motorway e-vignette (*e-matrica*) online or at the first petrol station before you join the motorway.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk Dobó István tér, climb to **Eger Castle** for the 1552 siege story and the casemates, then out to the 40 m Ottoman **minaret**, the northernmost surviving in Europe.
itinerary.evening: First pass through the **Szépasszony-völgy**, the horseshoe of cellar doors below the town. Do not try to do all of it. Pick three doors, drink small, and eat afterwards at **Macok Bistro & Wine Bar** under the castle wall.

itinerary.title: Egerszalók, Noszvaj and Bikavér Properly
itinerary.morning: **St. Andrea** at Egerszalók, 8 km southwest. Taste *Áldás* against *Lőrinc*, then go up the range; this is the cleanest introduction to what modern Eger is trying to be.
itinerary.afternoon: North to **Thummerer** at Noszvaj for the classical counterweight, deep tuff cellars, long-aged Bikavér Superior, and a family archive worth asking about.
itinerary.evening: Back to Egerszalók for the **Saliris** thermal complex and its travertine "salt hill", then a quiet dinner in Eger.

itinerary.title: Quarry, Fúzió and the Nagy-Eged Climb
itinerary.morning: **Bolyki**, a winery built into a disused rhyolite quarry on the town's edge, with tanks under the rock face. Taste the Kékfrankos and the Egri Csillag.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk or drive up **Nagy-Eged**, Eger's steep limestone hill and the region's most ambitious vineyard site, then down into town for **Gál Tibor Fúzió** on Széchenyi utca.
itinerary.evening: **Kovács Nimród** for the single-vineyard bottlings, then dinner at **Imola Udvarház** above the castle. Pack tonight; tomorrow is a relocation.

itinerary.title: East to Hegyalja: Mezőzombor and Mád
itinerary.morning: Drive Eger → Tokaj-Hegyalja on the M3 and route 37. Stop at **Disznókő** near Mezőzombor, the estate at the region's western gate, with the modern Makovecz-school winery building and a tasting that lays out aszú against dry Furmint.
itinerary.afternoon: Into **Mád**. Walk up to the **Szent Tamás** and **Betsek** slopes for the lie of the land: south-facing, volcanic, terraced.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Percz** in Mád, Hungarian cooking with a serious Hegyalja list.

itinerary.title: Mád: Szepsy, Royal Tokaji, Barta
itinerary.morning: **Szepsy István**, by appointment. The dry Furmints from Szent Tamás and Úrágya are the reference point for the whole region's shift toward dry wine.
itinerary.afternoon: **Royal Tokaji**'s Mád cellar for the first-growth aszú range, then **Barta** in the Rákóczi cellar beneath Kővágó, whose terraced Öreg Király vineyard was rebuilt from scrub.
itinerary.evening: **First Estate** in Mád for dinner, or back to Percz. If it is late October, ask anyone whether the aszú pickers are still out, a second and third pass through the same rows can run into November.

itinerary.title: Tarcal and Tokaj Town
itinerary.morning: **Gróf Degenfeld** at Tarcal, manor, park and a broad range including szamorodni. Then the short climb to the Tarcal hillside for the view over the Bodrog plain.
itinerary.afternoon: Lunch at **Sárga Borház** on the Tarcal slope, then into **Tokaj** town itself for **Demeter Zoltán**, a one-man cellar in the old town, and a walk to the Bodrog-Tisza confluence.
itinerary.evening: Stay in Tarcal or Tokaj. Order **halászlé** and drink dry Furmint with it; the sweet wines come after the fish, not with it.

itinerary.title: Tolcsva, Sárospatak and Out
itinerary.morning: **Oremus** at **Tolcsva**, Vega Sicilia's Tokaj estate, with a long cellar system and a rigorous tasting; ask for Mandolás alongside the aszú.
itinerary.afternoon: Lunch at **Gusteau** in Tolcsva, the region's most consistent kitchen. Then 20 km to **Sárospatak** for the Rákóczi castle if you have the hours.
itinerary.evening: Out via **Debrecen** (100 km) or back to Budapest (240 km, ~2 h 40). Buy at the cellars, not at the airport: EU-bound flights allow a case in hold luggage and estates ship.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Senator-Ház
accommodationStrategy.description: on the main square, 300 m from the castle ramp, and walkable to Macok and the taxi rank you need for a Szépasszony-völgy evening. No car use after tasting.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3-5 weeks ahead; Eger fills for the September Bikavér events.

accommodationStrategy.name: Botrytis Hotel or a Mád guesthouse
accommodationStrategy.description: Mád puts Szepsy, Royal Tokaji, Barta, Holdvölgy, Percz and the Szent Tamás slope inside a 2 km radius, so the densest tasting day of the week needs no driving at all.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4-6 weeks ahead; harvest weekends go first.

accommodationStrategy.name: Gróf Degenfeld Castle Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: sleeping on a working Tokaj estate, with a park, a restaurant and the vineyard behind the house; a good last two nights and an easy run to Debrecen.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6-8 weeks ahead direct, bundled with a tasting.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming applies. Coverage is solid in Eger and along route 37; thinner in the Zemplén side valleys above Tolcsva.
logistics.emergency: 112. Pharmacies are *gyógyszertár*; Eger and Sátoraljaújhely have the nearest hospitals to Hegyalja.
logistics.weather: October swings 6-20 °C in a day, and Hegyalja mornings are foggy, that river fog off the Bodrog is precisely what makes botrytis possible. Cellars sit at 10-12 °C year-round; take a jacket.
logistics.bookingWindows: Szepsy and Demeter Zoltán 3-6 weeks; Barta, Holdvölgy, Oremus, Disznókő and Royal Tokaji 5-10 days; St. Andrea and Thummerer 2-3 days; Gusteau and Percz a week in harvest season.
logistics.money: forint, not euro, at roughly 390-410 HUF to €1. Cards work at estates and restaurants; carry cash for Szépasszony-völgy cellar doors, some of which still take notes only. Refuse dynamic currency conversion on card terminals.
logistics.transportRules: **Hungary enforces a 0.00 blood-alcohol limit**, no glass of wine, no beer, no exceptions, and roadside checks are routine in wine regions during harvest. Either nominate a non-drinking driver each day or hire a local driver for the two heavy tasting days (roughly €90, €140 per day). Motorways require an **e-matrica** vignette bought in advance by number plate; on the 2026 D1 tariff a 10-day national pass is 6,900 HUF (~€17.50), a monthly 11,170 HUF (~€28) and an annual 61,760 HUF, with a single day at 5,550 HUF. County-only vignettes are 7,190 HUF each for the year and cover Heves and Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén far more cheaply if you avoid the M3, though two of them together cost more than a 10-day national pass, so for one week take the national one.
logistics.permits: none for cellar visits. Vineyard walking is generally tolerated on tracks but never between rows during harvest, ask at the cellar first.

proTips: Do the Szépasszony-völgy on your first evening, not your last. It is a cellar row, not a fine-wine destination, treating it as orientation rather than climax saves the week's palate.
In Tokaj, taste **dry Furmint first, aszú last**, and ask for a **szamorodni** in between. Going straight to the sweet wine wastes the region's best current argument.
Ask every Hegyalja cellar for the *dűlő*. Szent Tamás, Betsek, Úrágya and Király are the names that separate a good bottle from a great one, and the answer is usually on the back label.
Base in **Mád**, not Tokaj town. Tokaj has the name and the confluence; Mád has the producers, and you can walk to five of them.
Book Szepsy before you book flights. It is the single hardest appointment in the region and the rest of the week can be arranged around it.
Time Day 7 for late October and you may catch **aszú picking**, two or three passes through the same rows, berry by berry. Ask a cellar whether you can walk out with the pickers for an hour.
Learn *"Egészségedre"* (cheers) and *"Egy pohár száraz furmintot kérek"* (a glass of dry Furmint, please). Tipping is 10-12%, and increasingly added to the bill, check before doubling it.

raw.Appellations and classifications: **Eger PDO** (*Egri* DHC): **Egri Bikavér** is a red blend led by Kékfrankos, with Bikavér **Superior** and **Grand Superior** as tightened tiers, lower yields, longer ageing, and at Grand Superior level a single named *dűlő* (vineyard) on the label. **Egri Csillag** is the white counterpart, a multi-variety blend built on Carpathian Basin grapes. **Tokaj-Hegyalja PDO** covers 27 settlements on the volcanic foothills of the Zemplén. **Aszú** is made from individually picked botrytised berries (*Botrytis cinerea*) kneaded into a base wine; since the 2013 vintage the legal minimum sits at the old 5-puttonyos level, so *puttonyos* on a label is now optional shorthand rather than the grading it once was. **Szamorodni** ("as it came") is pressed from whole bunches, dry or sweet; **fordítás** is a second wine drawn from already-pressed aszú paste. The black fur on Hegyalja cellar walls is **Cladosporium cellaris**, and it is a sign of correct humidity, not neglect.
raw.Reservation-only cellars: **Szepsy István** (Mád) and **Demeter Zoltán** (Tokaj) are appointment-only and can be booked out weeks ahead; **Barta** (Mád, in the Rákóczi cellar under Kővágó hill) and **Holdvölgy** (Mád) run booked tasting programmes, not drop-in bars. **Royal Tokaji**, **Disznókő** (Mezőzombor) and **Oremus** (Tolcsva) take scheduled visits, still best booked 5-10 days out. In Eger, **St. Andrea** (Egerszalók), **Thummerer** (Noszvaj) and **Kovács Nimród** want a day or two's notice; **Bolyki** and **Gál Tibor Fúzió** in town are walk-in-friendly.
raw.Producers and wines to ask for: Eger: **St. Andrea**, *Áldás* (Egri Csillag) and *Lőrinc* (an approachable Bikavér), then the Nagy-Eged bottlings if the cellar will pour them. **Thummerer** for the classic Superior style, **Gál Tibor** for Fúzió and Kékfrankos, **Kovács Nimród** for single-vineyard Battonage Chardonnay and Syrah, **Bolyki** for the quarry site as much as the wine. Tokaj: **Szepsy** for dry Furmint that redefines the region, **Royal Tokaji** for its first-growth range, **Disznókő** for aszú with clarity, **Oremus** for Mandolás dry Furmint, **Gróf Degenfeld** at Tarcal, **Barta** for terraced Öreg Király, **Holdvölgy** and **Demeter Zoltán** for small-scale precision.
raw.First-growth vineyards: The 1737 royal classification named the crus you will hear about all week: **Szent Tamás** and **Betsek** above Mád, **Úrágya** on the Mád-Tarcal ridge, **Király** at Mád/Tarcal, with Nyulászó, Percze and Mézes Mály close behind. Ask which *dűlő* a bottle came from; in Hegyalja the answer is the wine.
raw.Signature dishes: **Halászlé** (river-fish soup, paprika-red, Tisza style with carp), **töltött káposzta** (stuffed cabbage), **Mangalica** (the curly-haired pig, best as a slow-cooked shoulder or cured *szalonna*), **körözött** (sheep's-cheese and paprika spread, the standard cellar snack), and **somlói galuska** for pudding.
